claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

1. **How many children do you have (or are responsible for)?** And what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 18 now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. You're asking about your son Alex who is 18 years old.

Since Alex is 18, he's over the age of 16, so there are specific rules that apply. For children aged 16-20, you can normally still qualify for Child Benefit if they stay in approved education or training.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he in sixth form, college, or an approved training program?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's still in college doing his A-levels.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. Since Alex is 18 and in college doing his A-levels, that counts as approved education, which is good for eligibility purposes.

Now I need to understand your living situation and responsibility for Alex:

**Does Alex live with you, or do you contribute financially towards his upkeep** (such as for food, clothes, or pocket money)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He doesn't live with me anymore, but I do help out financially - I contribute towards his upkeep.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex doesn't live with you but you contribute financially towards his upkeep, this is relevant to your eligibility.

**How much do you contribute towards Alex's upkeep, and how often do you make these contributions?** (For example, weekly, monthly, or in lump sums)

I'm asking because to continue receiving Child Benefit when a child lives elsewhere, you generally need to contribute at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment itself.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I contribute about £26 a week towards his costs - things like clothes, food, that sort of thing.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Contributing £26 a week towards Alex's costs for things like clothes and food is helpful information.

Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. And one final question to complete my assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, no one else is claiming for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! **You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

- Alex is 18 and in college doing his A-levels, which counts as approved education. You can continue to receive Child Benefit for children under 20 who stay in approved education or training.

- Even though Alex doesn't live with you anymore, you're contributing £26 per week towards his upkeep (for clothes, food, etc.). This meets the requirement that you contribute at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment itself (which is currently £25.60 per week for the eldest/only child).

- You live in the UK and no one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

Since you meet all the eligibility criteria, you should be able to claim Child Benefit for Alex while he continues in his approved education.

**Important note:** Please be aware that if either you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge. You can still claim Child Benefit, but you might need to pay back some or all of it through the tax system.
